keyFindings.description: FindMarks/markSearch is a second implementation of FindMark's quote rule (span joining, block separator, pending empty runs, first span only, NUL replacement) and MarkAttrs' first-mark rule, while FindMark and MarkAttrs stay in production (docs/marks.go applySuggestion 249/253, suggestion read 223, unmarkExpired 875). A later change to one copy does not reach the other, and refresh and applySuggestion then read different quotes. Fix: FindMark and MarkAttrs become one-key FindMarks lookups; today's FindMark/MarkAttrs bodies move into find_marks_test.go as frozen oracles (as ytext_ranges_test.go keeps frozenYTextRanges); readAnchored goes back to FindMark.

yFragmentLocations (1201-1269) copies walk.go's position rules (opaque = text or leaf, doc adds no boundary tokens, others add 2, leaf counts 1) so ProseMirror positions are defined twice; a change to walk/nodeSize misplaces marks silently. Fix: extract the opaque and boundary-token rules into walk.go helpers used by walkNode, nodeSize and yFragmentLocations.

FindMarks clones each found mark's attrs (line 809) on every write for refreshAnchors and readAnchored, which never read Attrs; ReplaceText's consumer (MarkWriter.Mark via markAttributeValue) already copies. New avoidable per-anchor allocation on the hot path. Fix: keep mark.Attrs uncloned and document MarkFound.Attrs as read-only.

markQuoteInTxn builds a one-use pmdoc.NewMarkWriter through writeQuoteMark (141), leaving pmdoc.MarkRange with no production caller. Fix: markQuoteInTxn calls documentSchemaError(pmdoc.MarkRange(...)) as at base, and ReplaceText calls documentSchemaError(writer.Mark(...)) directly; delete writeQuoteMark.
